text: . India’s equity benchmarks retreated this week after two consecutive weekly gains, as lingering uncertainty in the Middle East and ​elevated crude oil prices tempered risk appetite for stocks. The Nifty 50 fell 0.8 percent this week to 24,366 and the 30 share Sensex at Bombay Stock Exchange, lost 0.6 percent to 78,009.In the forex market, the Indian rupee closed the week with losses against the dollar. The rupee ended little changed at 95 rupees and 42 paise against the US dollar, yesterday but fell 0.2 percent from a week ago.

. In Canadian Open Tennis, seventh seed Iga Swiatek of Poland defeated second seed Elena Rybakina in straight sets to claim the Women’s Singles title in Toronto last night. Swiatek captured her first title of the season with a swift 6-2 6-3 win, giving her a confidence boost heading into the US Open.In Men’s Singles, American tennis player Ben Shelton won the title in Montreal by defeating fellow American Brandon Nakashima with a score of 6-3, 7-6(4). With this victory, the fifth-seeded Shelton successfully defended his tournament crown and captured his second career ATP Masters 1000 trophy. This victory marks his fourth tournament win of the 2026 season, following earlier titles in Dallas, Munich, and Stuttgart, bringing his total career tour-level titles to seven.

. The 12-day long annual Shri Buddha Amarnath Yatra 2026 to the ancient Baba Budha Amarnath Temple in Rajpura village of Mandi Tehsil in Poonch district is scheduled to begin tomorrow and will continue until August 28, 2026, culminating around Raksha Bandhan.The first batch of the pilgrims will depart from the Bhagwati Nagar Yatri Niwas in Jammu toward the border district of Poonch tomorrow. Authorities have enforced strict multi-tier security and surveillance across Poonch, Rajouri, and transit routes. The convoys of the devotees will move under police escort, with additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) deployed. District administration and local bodies have finalised arrangements, including water proof tents, community kitchen (Langar) locations, parking layouts, and health care stations along the pilgrimage route.The Poonch district administration launched a dedicated portal to facilitate advance registration for pilgrims coming from across the country. The Budha Amarnath Yatra is an annual Hindu pilgrimage held during the auspicious monsoon month of Shravan (July-August) to the ancient Baba Budha Amarnath Temple dedicated to Lord Shiva located in Rajpura village in Mandi Tehsil of Poonch district. The shrine sits 4 thousand 600 feet above sea level and features a self-manifested white stone Shivling.The journey traditionally commences from the Bhagwati Nagar base camp in Jammu, taking pilgrims about 230 km northwest into the mountainous terrain of Poonch. Devotees traditionally bathe in the nearby holy Pulastya River (named after Rishi Pulastya) before entering the temple for prayers. Many believe completing this yatra adds profound completeness to a devotee’s broader pilgrimage path to the higher-altitude Amarnath Cave shrine.

. Global crude oil prices declined today as investors assessed prospects for weaker ‌global demand this year and higher US crude stocks. Brent crude was trading 1.8 per cent down at 87 US dollars and 41 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.9 per cent down at 81 US dollars and 65 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.Meanwhile, the US commercial crude oil inventories increased by 17.4 million barrels to 424.4 million barrels in the week ended on 7th of August, according to data released by the Energy Information Administration. This marked the biggest weekly increase in oil inventories since January 2023.

. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that saree is not merely a piece of attire, rather a magnificent symbol of Indian culture. The Minister said this in a video message during Saree Shastra in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat underlined the mastery of wearing one saree in multiple ways, the craft of designing and weaving a single saree in diverse styles. Highlighting the tradition of representing culture through sarees, he said that exhibitions and events like this help spread awareness about India’s tradition of wearing and weaving sarees, and understanding which saree suits which occasion far and wide.Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse said that the exhibition serves as a prime example of presenting diverse states and culture through sarees. The Minister said that the exhibition brings together artists from across the country and aims to present their work through the medium of the saree. He said, it reflects the country’s rich culture, which is being conveyed through saree craftsmanship.Saree Shastra is a three-day exhibition to honour the women who weave, preserve and wear sarees. The event reimangines the saree as one of India’s most enduring cultural artefact.

. In Indonesia, the death toll has risen to 47 after a powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Flores today.The earthquake was followed by dozens of aftershocks as rescue teams continued efforts to reach the worst-affected areas. Hundreds of buildings in the region have been damaged by the quake and the dozens of aftershocks that followed. A 6.4 magnitude earthquake was also felt in North Sumatra later in the day, at a depth of 163 kilometres. Tsunami waves of less than one metre were reported in several parts of the country. The tsunami alert was withdrawn around three hours after the initial earthquake.Officials said people are still believed to be trapped inside buildings in several affected areas. Landslides have also been reported, with debris blocking roads and hampering rescue and relief operations.

. In Canadian Open Tennis, American Brandon Nakashima defeated Spain’s Rafael Jodar 7-6(3) 6-4 in the Men’s Singles semi-finals at Montreal, this morning to reach ‌the Canadian Open final. This puts the American one win away ​from his first Masters ​1000 title ahead of the ⁠U.S. Open.In the other semifinal, defending champion Ben Shelton has reached the finals in Montreal after defeating fellow American Learner Tien 6-2, 6-3 this morning. Shelton, who has yet to drop a single set in his entire title defense campaign, will face countryman Brandon Nakashima for the Masters 1000 trophy.In the Women’s Singles, fourth seed Coco Gauff defeated second seed Elena Rybakina in a grueling 2-hour and 50-minute blockbuster semifinal in Toronto this morning, winning 6-4, 6-7(8), 7-6(3). In another semi-final match, seventh seed Iga Świątek defeated ninth seed Elina Svitolina with a score of 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 in Toronto this morning.

. India emerged as the overall champions at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship by winning an impressive 35 medals after four days of competition held at Lagos in Nigeria. Indian contingent secured thirteen gold, eight silver, and fourteen bronze medals at the event across the Under 23 and senior competitions.The senior Indian fencers claimed five gold medals in six events on the fourth and final day of the competition, securing honours in Men’s Sabre, Women’s Sabre, Men’s E’pée, Women’s Epée and Women’s foil, as well as a silver in Men’s foil.The performance also helped India win the Wilkinson Sword Trophy, awarded by the Commonwealth Fencing Federation to the country with the best overall results. Secretary-general, Fencing Association of India, Rajeev Mehta, said in a statement that lifting the Commonwealth Overall Championship title for the first time is a testament to the talent, discipline, and hard work within Indian fencing.

. Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog, Ashok Kumar Lahiri today released a report titled Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub. The report highlights 12 priority sectors that hold strong potential for global competitiveness, local value addition, job creation, and deeper integration into global supply chains. It also lays down a strategic roadmap to strengthen India’s manufacturing ecosystem and support the vision of Viksit Bharat. The 12 key sectors shortlisted in the report are automobiles, electronics, steel, capital goods, defence and drones, chemicals, solar PV, textiles, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, telecom equipment, leather and footwear and food processing.Addressing the occasion, Dr Lahiri emphasized that manufacturing must play a significantly larger role to fulfill India’s long-term growth aspirations. He noted that economic development across most of the countries shows that sustained transformation is consistently driven by strong manufacturing and expanding exports. Highlighting towards the shifting international trends, Dr Lahiri stated that the global manufacturing landscape is undergoing rapid change as businesses actively seek to diversify their supply chains. He expressed confidence that the report will serve as a useful reference for policymakers, government, industry leaders, and researchers as they work together to strengthen India’s manufacturing ecosystem.

. The nation is celebrating the 80th Independence Day today. Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the celebrations at the iconic Red Fort in Delhi. The Celebrations  commemorated 150 years of the enduring legacy of the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’. For the first time, ‘Vande Mataram’ was rendered during the celebrations at Red Fort.Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, Prime Minister Modi said, the government is moving forward with the aim of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity by 2047. Mr. Modi said over the past 12 years, the determination and dedication of crores of citizens have helped take the country to new heights. He said 25 crore people have come out of poverty during this period. Mr Modi said India, once counted among the Fragile Five economies, has now emerged as a major and the fastest-growing economy in the world. He said India has set an ambitious goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047. On the occasion, the Prime Minister announced free online coaching for poor and middle-class families preparing for various public examinations. He also announced that the government will provide AI-skilling training to one crore youth over the next one year.Highlighting the government’s focus on critical minerals, Mr Modi said modern technology depends entirely on these minerals and India is actively working to secure its position in the sector. The Prime Minister said, energy security is one of the major requirements of the present times and the government has taken several significant steps in this direction. He said nuclear energy is an important means of ensuring a country’s energy security. Mr. Modi said the government is moving forward with the aim of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity by 2047.In his address, the Prime Minister called upon the nation to harness the seven streams of strength called as Sapt Dhara. He said, in the next five to seven years, the country will achieve all that could not be achieved in the past five to seven decades.

. Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi has informed that no decision has been taken by the Government to increase ethanol blending with petrol beyond 20 percent. In a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha, Mr Gopi said that any future decision regarding higher ethanol blends will be taken only after detailed scientific and technical studies and consultations with all relevant stakeholders, including automobile manufacturers and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).The Minister said that the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, OMCs  and technical institutions.He said, extensive laboratory studies and field trials covering parameters such as engine durability, emissions and fuel efficiency, have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards. The Minister added that these studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. The Minister said, these extensive laboratory studies, field validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged all parties to support the implementation of women’s reservation in Parliament and state assemblies without making it a political fight.In his Independence Day address to the nation from the ramparts of Red Fort, Mr Modi asked them to step forward to honour women and ensure that the country’s women secure 33 per cent representation in the Legislative Assemblies and the Lok Sabha as soon as possible. He said that women should be given the opportunity to contribute to shaping India’s policies.

. Sensex has registered a gain of 114 points to settle at 78,080 and Nifty declined 40 points to 24,396 today. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained over 0.1 per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index rose 0.3 per cent.The Sensex traded on a subdued note during the intra-day trade. However, it erased its losses and closed higher following the Closing Auction Session adjustment. The weekly expiry of the futures and options contracts of Sensex also added to the volatility. Conversely, the Nifty remained in the negative zone throughout the session amid lingering geopolitical uncertainties.In the Sensex pack, 19 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Indigo climbed 2.8 per cent, NTPC as well as Bharat Electronics Limited advanced two per cent and Larsen and Toubro added over 1.9 per cent. In contrast, ICICI Bank lost 1.3 per cent, Titan dipped one per cent and Reliance fell 0.8 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 17 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive zone. Among the top gainers, Telecommunication as well as FMCG added one per cent, Realty rose one and a half per cent and Services gained 0.8 per cent. In contrast, Metal declined nearly one per cent, Commodities as well as Insurance shed half a per cent and Top 10 Banks fell 0.2 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2,192 companies advanced, 2,127 declined and 226 remained unchanged.

. World leaders and foreign missions extended Independence Day greetings to India today, praising its democratic journey, civilisational heritage and expanding role in regional and global cooperation.U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio highlighted strengthening ties between India and the United States, while Singaporean President Tharman Shanmugaratnam cited growing cooperation in skills, digitalisation, sustainability and advanced manufacturing.Israeli Ambassador Reuven Azar, Argentine Ambassador Mariano Caucino, Sri Lankan High Commissioner Mahishini Colonné, Nepal’s embassy, the French Embassy, Australia’s deputy high commissioner and Canada’s high commission also conveyed greetings, emphasising India’s heritage, diversity, economic potential and growing bilateral ties.Former Maldivian President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and Maldives National Party President Mohamed Nazim praised India’s development and its close partnership with the Maldives.This year’s celebrations highlighted 150 years of the national song “Vande Mataram” and the aspirations and contributions of India’s youth toward building a developed India by 2047.

. Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today interacted with MY Bharat-NSS volunteers during the Independence Day celebrations in New Delhi. Addressing the volunteers, Dr Mandaviya appreciated their contribution towards social service and encouraged them to actively participate in initiatives aimed at building a Viksit Bharat. He emphasised that the energy, commitment and innovative ideas of young people are essential for achieving the vision of a developed and self-reliant India.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the programme also provided a platform for volunteers to share their experiences, ideas and aspirations. The interaction reaffirmed the commitment of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to provide meaningful opportunities for youth participation and leadership in nation-building. Around 500 students participated in the event, showcasing patriotism, national unity and collective participation.

. Lok Sabha has passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. When the House met at 3:00 PM after the second adjournment, Union Coal and Mines Minister G Kishan Reddy moved the Bill to further amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. The bill aims to make India’s mining sector more efficient, investment-friendly and well-equipped to fulfil the country’s growing demand for critical minerals. The Bill was passed without discussion amid opposition uproar.

. The Technology Development Board today signed an agreement with a private medical device company from Visakhapatnam for commercialisation of indigenous AI-Powered cervical cancer screening technology. The agreement will support the manufacturing and commercialization of GrivaVision, an indigenously developed, portable digital colposcope with AI-assisted capabilities for early detection of cervical pre-cancerous lesions. Through the Board’s support, the company will establish manufacturing capabilities at Kollam, Kerala, enabling commercial-scale production and wider deployment of the technology. The initiative seeks to make cervical cancer screening more accessible and affordable, particularly across primary and community healthcare settings. GrivaVision integrates a high-definition camera, an in-built display, user-friendly interface that assists gynaecologists in identifying pre-cancerous abnormalities during routine clinical examinations.

. Baloch leader Mir Yar Baloch has accused the Pakistani military of committing war crimes and targeting civilians, claiming that video footage from the recent airstrikes in Surab provides evidence of military aggression against the local population in Balochistan. In a social media post, Mir Yar Baloch said, he plans to approach the International Criminal Court (ICC) over the Pakistani military operation in the Gidar Goandhan area of Surab on Tuesday, which resulted in the deaths of 30 civilians, including women, children, and infants.Meanwhile, the situation in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, PoJK remains tense, with protesters raising concerns about recent controversial elections conducted under the influence of Pakistani force, targetted killings and forced disappearances of innocent people and essential supply disruptions. Jammu and Kashmir Joint Action Committee (JKJAAC) senior leader Sardar Shabir has claimed that around 100 people had been killed by Pakistani forces during the unrest in the occupied territory.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.4 per cent up at 1,53,419 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, Silver rose 0.8 per cent to 2,37, 214 rupees per kilogram.

. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio extended congratulations to the people of India on Independence Day. In his message, Mr Rubio said that the India-US relationship continues to grow and is stronger than ever, thanks to the personal relationship between US President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.He added that bilateral collaboration is making both nations and the broader Indian Ocean region safer, stronger, and more prosperous. He further stated that the deep ties of friendship and family between people from both countries form the foundation of a partnership that is innovative, resilient, and forward-looking. He said the US looks forward to the future the two countries will build together.External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar thanked Secretary Rubio for his warm wishes. Dr Jaishankar also expressed gratitude to his counterparts from Australia, Slovakia, Cyprus, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Singapore for their Independence Day wishes.

. Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr L Murugan today said Government has established a Fact Check Unit in Press Information Bureau to mitigate fake news related to its programmes and policies. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, DR Murugan informed that the Fact Check Unit verifies claims relating to Government Ministries, Departments, PSUs and other Central Government organisations through a structured fact-checking process. It disseminates verified information through various platforms.The MoS further stated that Doordarshan and Akashvani further disseminate verified information through their news bulletins, programmes and digital platforms. DD News follows a multi-layered editorial mechanism involving rigorous fact-checking, cross-verification through multiple credible sources and editorial scrutiny before broadcast. PIB Fact Check content is regularly integrated into Doordarshan and Akashvani news and digital platforms to counter misinformation and false narratives.PIB, as the principal information dissemination agency of the Government, facilitates timely, credible and accurate communication in different forms through various media platforms. Prasar Bharati plays a key role in fulfilling the mandate of public service broadcasting. Information is disseminated in multiple languages, including regional languages and dialects, using various platforms.

. On World Elephant Day, Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav, today said that Project Elephant reflects India’s commitment to protecting elephants, conserving their habitats and promoting harmonious coexistence between elephants and communities. In a social media post, Mr Yadav said that under Project Elephant, various measures are being implemented, including early warning systems and AI-based alerts to keep communities informed, solar-powered fences and trenches to protect people and elephants, and timely compensation for crop losses suffered by farmers. He added that the railways are also adopting warning signals, AI-based solutions and speed restrictions in critical corridors to prevent elephant deaths. The Minister also said that the government is promoting education and awareness to encourage communities to live in harmony with elephants.

. Indian embassies and consulates marked India’s 80th Independence Day today with flag-hoisting ceremonies, cultural programs and community gatherings. Thousands of Indian nationals and diaspora members joined celebrations in Singapore, China and Hong Kong, underscoring India’s strong people-to-people ties with the region.In Singapore, High Commissioner Shilpak Ambule hoisted the tricolour before more than 2,500 diaspora members. The ceremony included the national anthem, “Vande Mataram,” patriotic songs and excerpts from President Droupadi Murmu’s address.In Beijing, Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami hoisted the tricolour at the Indian Embassy before a large diaspora gathering despite heavy rain. He later read Murmu’s address and presented prizes to winners of Independence Day competitions.In Hong Kong, the Indian Association hosted a gala attended by Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu, Consul General Rajesh Naik and community leaders. Lee praised the Indian community’s contribution to Hong Kong, while Naik highlighted growing economic ties and India’s growth, technological advances and inclusive development under the Viksit Bharat vision.

. National Testing Agency (NTA) will release the provisional answer keys for UGC-NET June 2026, CSIR-NET, ICAR-All India Entrance Examination for Admission and All India Competitive Examination for Ph.D. programmes today. In a social media post, NTA said, the provisional answer keys will be published on its website. It advised candidates to rely only on official communication from NTA.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast very heavy rainfall today at places over Arunachal Pradesh, Gangetic West Bengal, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Parts of north-east India, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Gilgit, Baltistan, Jharkhand, Konkan and Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh are also likely to receive moderate to heavy rainfall during the day.The Met Department also predicted thunderstorms and lightning today in places over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, Gangetic West Bengal, North Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Similar weather conditions are also expected over Coastal Karnataka, Odisha, South Interior Karnataka, Sub Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and Telangana.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has extended best wishes to all the people belonging to the Parsi community on the occasion of Parsi New Year, Navroz. In a social media post, the Vice President prayed that this new year brings peace, prosperity and happiness to every family and inspires all to strengthen the bonds of unity, harmony and brotherhood in the nation. Mr Radhakrishnan wished that the timeless values of faith, compassion and service continue to enrich India’s shared heritage and guide countrymen towards a brighter future.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also extended greetings to the countrymen on the occasion of Parsi New Year Navroz. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that the Parsi community’s remarkable contribution across sectors has enriched the nation in countless ways. The Prime Minister wished that this year ahead be filled with peace, joy, prosperity and good health for everyone.

. In Chess, World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen has won Esports World Cup title for the second year in a row, by defeating Belarusian Grandmaster Denis Lazavik 2-0 in Paris, France. Representing Team Liquid, the 35-year-old Norwegian remained completely undefeated throughout the entire tournament.Meanwhile, American Grandmaster Hikaru Nakamura secured third place after defeating Alireza Firouzja 4-1 in a chaotic bronze-medal match that was repeatedly disrupted by technical problems and internet disconnections. The championship layout followed a best-of-three sets format, where the first two sets featured four games each, and a final two-game set was reserved as a tiebreaker if needed.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has announced to provide free online coaching for students belonging to poor and middle class families. In his address to the nation, Mr Modi said, the move is aimed at easing the financial burden of aspirants preparing for competitive exams. He said, this is a revolutionary step towards making quality education accessible to everyone, led by top teachers. He said, this will save thousands of crore rupees of middle-class family in coaching classes.The Prime Minister said that the government has decided that one crore youth will be given training in AI skilling in the next one year. He said this will enable them to take the lead in the global AI sector. Mr Modi said the country has to focus on three things – cost, quality and skill.Prime Minister said a talent hunt will be launched across villages, cities and schools to identify talent among children aged five to 15 years. He said, the children’s talent will be identified, and they will be given special training to help them become good players for the country. He said, today India is making its place in the world of sports. Mr Modi said, in 2030, India will host the Commonwealth Games.

. The Report of the Inquiry Committee investigating allegations concerning former Allahabad High Court Judge Yashwant Varma was tabled in both the Houses of Parliament. In the Lok Sabha, Secretary General Uttpal Kuma Singh tabled the Hindi and English versions of the Report of the Inquiry Committee constituted under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 as well as the Oral and documentary evidence recorded during the course of the inquiry. While in the Rajya Sabha, the report in this regard was tabled by Secretary General P C Mody.The Judges Inquiry Committee, investigating allegations concerning Yashwant Varma, had submitted its report to the Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in May this year. The Committee was constituted by Mr Birla on 12th of August last year to probe the allegations levelled against Justice Varma, after a sum of burnt cash was found at his official residence in New Delhi.

. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and the Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) have confirmed that Afghanistan will host India for a three-match T20 International series at the Arun Jaitley Cricket Stadium in Delhi from 13 to 17th next month. The series is part of Afghanistan’s Future Tours Program and will be played in India, where Afghanistan has hosted its home fixtures in recent years.BCCI President, Mithun Manhas said, BCCI remains committed to supporting the growth of cricket in Afghanistan and providing its players with opportunities to compete at the highest level.BCCI Honorary Secretary, Devajit Saikia said, the BCCI is pleased to support the Afghanistan Cricket Board in hosting this T20 International series in India.Afghanistan most recently toured India for a three-match ODI series in June this year, while the two sides also played a three-match T20 International series in January 2024.India hosted Afghanistan for their historic first Test in 2018, and the two teams have since continued to engage regularly across formats.

. In Men’s Cricket, India were 288 for 2 in their first innings at stumps on day one of the first Test against hosts Srilanka at Galle International Cricket Stadium. Earlier, India won the toss and opted to bat first.Devdutt Padikkal remained unbeaten on 131 while Rishabh Pant was on 27 when stumps were drawn this evening. KL Rahul retired hurt on 77. Today’s game was cut short to 73 overs due to two rain breaks.

. Ahead of Independence Day, a platform for creative expression has been provided to the youth in Uttar Pradesh. For this, the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign was launched. Under this campaign, the graffiti wall programme organised near Lucknow University today. Artists from the city painted public murals on the theme of a mafia-free and changing Uttar Pradesh. Through these paintings, the Uttar Pradesh of before 2017 and the changes that have taken place in Uttar Pradesh thereafter were portrayed.On the wall, artists used their colours and imagination to portray in paintings the changed positive environment in the state in terms of law and order, infrastructure and opportunities for youth. Young painter Manish Saroj’s painting expressed the pain of Uttar Pradesh suffering under mafia rule before 2017, while also presenting a positive picture of the change taking place now.Under the campaign, a comic distribution and dialogue programme will be organised in Muzaffarnagar tomorrow. During this, an original comic based on communal harmony will be distributed. Along with this, dialogues will also be held with youth in schools. On August 14, the song ‘Azadi from Fear’ of the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign will be launched. It will also feature a confluence of rap, music and digital art.

. In Hockey, India defeated Wales 3-1 today in a Group D match of the FIH Hockey World Cup in Amstelveen, Netherlands.  For India, captain Harmanpreet Singh scored two goals, while Sanjay Rana scored one. Sam Welsh scored the lone goal for Wales.

. In the Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index gained almost 3.6 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose around 1.2 per cent.Among the major European indices, Germany’s DAX was trading 0.4 per cent up, while London’s FTSE 100 dropped 0.3 per cent, when reports last came in. On economic front, United Kingdom’s real gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have increased by 0.4 per cent in April to June quarter of this year, down from growth of 0.6 per cent in the first quarter. Meanwhile, GDP grew by 0.3 per cent in June, after registering no growth in the previous month, according to the GDP figures released today by the Office for National Statistics.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves rose by 14.1 billion US dollars (USD) to 707 billion US dollars during the week ended August 7. According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 9.9 billion USD to 574.6 billion USD during the week.Gold reserves added 3.9 billion USD to 108.7 billion US dollars. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund was up by 116 million USD to around 4.9 billion USD. Special Drawing Rights increased by 79 million USD to 18.74 billion USD.

. World leaders and foreign missions today extended the 80th Independence Day greetings to India, praising its democratic journey, civilizational heritage and expanding role in regional and global cooperation.U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio highlighted the strengthening strategic partnership between India and the United States, while Singaporean President Tharman Shanmugaratnam underscored growing cooperation in skills development, digitalization, sustainability and advanced manufacturing.French President Emmanuel Macron also conveyed his warm wishes to India on its 80th Independence Day. Israeli President Isaac Herzog congratulated President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the people of India, sharing his message in Hindi as well.Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah extended his greetings and best wishes, while Latvia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs wished India continued progress, unity and prosperity.Greetings also came from Israeli Ambassador Reuven Azar, Argentine Ambassador Mariano Caucino, Sri Lankan High Commissioner Mahishini Colonné, the Embassy of Nepal, the French Embassy, Australia’s Deputy High Commissioner and Canada’s High Commission. Their messages highlighted India’s heritage and diversity, economic potential and expanding bilateral ties.Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu joined the global chorus of greetings, saying eight decades of independence reflected India’s aspirations, resilience and enduring spirit.Former Maldivian President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and Maldives National Party President Mohamed Nazim also praised India’s development and its close relationship with the Maldives.This year’s Independence Day celebrations also highlighted 150 years of the national song “Vande Mataram” and the aspirations and contributions of India’s youth toward the vision of building a developed India by 2047.

. The nation pays homage to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on his death anniversary today. The BJP stalwart had breathed his last on this day in 2018. Vajpayee served as the Prime Minister on three occasions. His first term was for only 13 days in 1996. He served his second term for a period of eleven months from 1998 to 1999 and then a full term from 1999 to 2004. He was awarded India’s highest civilian honour – Bharat Ratna – in 2015. Dignitaries will pay floral tributes to the former Prime Minister at his memorial Sadaiv Atal in the National Capital.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla paid tributes to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, on his death anniversary. In a social media post, the Lok Sabha Speaker noted that Mr Vajpayee was such a titan of Indian politics whose personality embodied a unique confluence of patriotism, democratic values, sensitivity, and extraordinary oratory. He added that over a parliamentary career spanning more than five decades, he was elected to the Lok Sabha ten times and to the Rajya Sabha twice. Mr Birla said that the former Prime Minister will always be remembered as a fiery parliamentarian, a powerful orator, an accomplished journalist, and a sensitive poet.He further underlined that as Prime Minister, Mr Vajpayee not only strengthened India’s democratic traditions but also gave a new direction to the country’s foreign policy and global role. Mr Birla added that his leadership was inspired by the vision of a strong, self-confident, and modern India that advances firmly on the world stage, rooted in its glorious civilisation and democratic values.Further, the Lok Sabha Speaker noted that Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s personality, thoughts, and ideals will forever guide coming generations on the path of national service, good governance, and democratic values.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also remembered former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on his death anniversary. Sharing a social media post, Mr Modi called Mr Vajpayee an extraordinary statesman blessed with remarkable vision, who dedicated his life to the service of the nation. He added that the words and efforts of the former Prime Minister inspired generations and his leadership strengthened the nation. Mr Modi added that Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s focus on good governance and public welfare will always continue to guide countrymen.Union Home Minister Amit Shah also paid homage to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee via a social media post. Mr Shah said that Atal Bihari Vajpayee was a patriot politician of such calibre who dedicated every moment of his life to the service of the nation. He added that on one hand, he made the entire world aware of India’s strength through nuclear tests and the Kargil War, while on the other hand, his value-based politics brought the vision of Antyodaya and good governance to the ground for the first time.Mr Shah noted that the towering personality and leadership of the former Prime Minister will continue to inspire every BJP worker towards nation-building forever.

. Romania has begun a controlled shutdown of the second reactor at its Cernavoda nuclear power plant as severe drought continues to affect much of Europe. Plant operator Nuclearelectrica said scorching temperatures and weeks of below-average rainfall have pushed the Danube River to record-low levels. The conditions forced the plant to shut down its first reactor in late July this year.The plant accounts for around 20 per cent of Romania’s electricity generation when operating at full capacity.Meanwhile, the country’s Ministry of Energy has said the country’s electricity needs can be met through alternative sources and imports following the shutdown of the second reactor.

. In Canadian Open Tennis, second seed Elena Rybakina will take on seventh seed Iga Swiatek in Women’s Singles title clash at Toronto tomorrow.Kazakhstan’s Rybakina defeated fourth seeded American Coco Gauff by 5-7,6-2,6-2 while Polish player Swiatek overpowered Elina Svitolina of Ukraine by 6-3,1-6, 6-3 in the semi-finals today.In Men’s Singles, defending champion Ben Shelton will face Brandon Nakashima in an All American final at Montreal tomorrow. Fifth seed Shelton secured a 6-2, 6-3 victory over fellow American and 12th seed Learner Tien while 28th seed Nakashima beat Spanish teenager and 20th seed Rafael Jodar 7-6(3) 6-4 to reach his first Masters 1000 final.

. Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan will be on a two-day visit to Tamil Nadu beginning today. During the visit, he will participate in a series of academic, commemorative, and literary events in Chennai, Chengalpattu, Thiruvarur, and Thanjavur.Today, Mr Radhakrishnan will attend the 22nd Convocation of the SRM Institute of Science and Technology in Chengalpattu. He will also attend the first death anniversary function of former Governor of Nagaland, Manipur and West Bengal, in Chennai. Later, the Vice-President will attend the release of the book ‘Echoes of a Nationalist Mind’ in Chennai. The book is based on the thoughts and writings of the late K. Ramagopalan, founder of Hindu Munnani.Tomorrow, the Vice-President will attend the 11th Convocation of the Central University of Tamil Nadu in Thiruvarur. He will thereafter participate in the Ruby and Silver Jubilee Valedictory Celebrations of SASTRA Deemed University at Thanjavur.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that public capital should act as a catalyst for private investment, rather than a substitute for it. Addressing a seminar in Jaipur on the role of the New Development Bank in mobilising private capital in BRICS member countries, Mrs. Sitharaman said BRICS economies are among the major engines of global growth, but they also face challenges in attracting private capital.She said that besides ensuring the availability of capital, it is equally important to build investor confidence, maintain stability and provide a predictable, long-term policy framework.The Finance Minister highlighted the role of multilateral development banks in reducing investment risks, making projects more financially viable and strengthening investor confidence, thereby helping mobilise private capital on a larger scale.Referring to India’s experience, Mrs. Sitharaman said the Central Government has strengthened the country’s infrastructure through sustained public capital expenditure and structural reforms.New Development Bank President Dilma Rousseff also addressed the seminar.Earlier, Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur said that increasing private capital participation is an important need in the current economic environment.The seminar is being held as part of the BRICS Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ meeting in Jaipur under India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, with the objective of strengthening cooperation on global economic and financial issues.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 10 paise to end at 95 rupees and 44 paise against the US dollar.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.

. President Droupadi Murmu hosted a State Reception at Rashtrapati Bhavan on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day yesterday.Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Former President Ram Nath Kovind, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Union Ministers, diplomats, eminent people from different walks of life and beneficiaries of various government programmes attended the Reception. This year’s Reception celebrated the rich and vibrant art and culture, timeless traditions and cuisine of Chhattisgarh, Goa, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

. The first-of-its-kind SURYAPATH TIRANGA Global Relay concluded yesterday, completing its journey from Fiji in the East to the United States in the West, across 54 countries and multiple time zones. The External Affairs Ministry said that the Suryapath Tiranga initiative was celebrated as part of the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign.Launched from the High Commission of India in Fiji, the relay carried the spirit of the Tiranga from one sunrise to the next, bringing together the Indian community and friends of India across the world. The relay ended with the flag hoisting by the Consulate General of India in San Francisco. The relay also marked 150 years of Vande Mataram, celebrating its enduring legacy as a symbol of India’s national spirit and pride.The relay witnessed overwhelming participation and response from the members of the diaspora, underscoring the deep emotional connection with the Tiranga.

. Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa bounced back from his previous-round defeat to secure a convincing victory over Dutch player Jorden Van Foreest in the fourth round of the Sinquefield Cup.The win took Praggnanandhaa’s tally to two-and-a-half points from four games, placing him in a share of second position in the 10-player, nine-round tournament.Praggnanandhaa had suffered a defeat against Germany’s Vincent Keymer in the previous round. His latest victory will boost his confidence and strengthen his bid for a podium finish.The Sinquefield Cup is part of the Grand Chess Tour, with a strong performance in the tournament also crucial for players seeking qualification for the Grand Chess Tour finale.

. Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today informed that around 440 space technology startups are registered in India. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Dr Singh said Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, NGEs to carry out various space activities. Out of these, 18 NGEs are start-ups. The Minister said the Government has undertaken several proactive measures following the liberalization of the space sector. This is being done to promote participation of startups in satellite manufacturing, launch services, downstream applications and space-based technologies. IN-SPACe is facilitating the transfer of available ISRO technologies to industry while also identifying and consolidating the technology requirements of industry for future technology development and transfer. Till date, 118 Technology Transfer Agreements have been executed.

. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio extended congratulations to the people of India on Independence Day. In his message, Mr Rubio said that the India-US relationship continues to grow and is stronger than ever, thanks to the personal relationship between US President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He added that bilateral collaboration is making both of nations, and the broader Indian Ocean region, safer, stronger, and more prosperous. He further stated that the deep ties of friendship and family between people from both countries form the foundation of a partnership that is innovative, resilient, and forward-looking. He said the US looks forward to the future the two countries will build together.External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar thanked Secretary Rubio for his warm wishes. Dr Jaishankar also expressed gratitude to his counterparts from Australia, Slovakia, Cyprus, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Singapore for their Independence Day wishes.

. At least eleven people were reportedly killed in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon today. Lebanon’s National News Agency reported that one of the airstrikes hit a home in Ansar village killing seven people. Another strike on the village of Deir al-Zahrani killed four people while injured 17. Israel’s military said, it had struck Hezbollah terror infrastructure in response to what it described as an earlier action against its soldiers. Lebanon’s Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned the attacks, saying the people killed were not military infrastructure.The attack is among the deadliest reported in Lebanon since the country agreed to a US-mediated peace framework with Israel. Under the arrangement, Israeli troops are to remain in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed and the Lebanese army takes control of the area. Hezbollah, which is backed by Iran, has rejected the terms, describing them as unacceptable.

. The country’s total exports, including merchandise and services are estimated at 80.14 billion US dollars in July this year, registering a robust 13.3 per cent year-on-year growth. According to the provisional data released by the Commerce Ministry, the export performance was led by merchandise shipments, which jumped over 19.6 per cent to 44.24 billion US dollars from a year earlier. The growth in merchandise exports was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering goods, organic and inorganic chemicals, cotton yarn and handloom products. Country’s merchandise trade deficit widened by 31.5 per cent year-on-year to 15 billion US dollars last month.Cumulatively, merchandise exports during April to July period of the current financial year are estimated at 173.78 billion US dollars, registering an increase of 17 per cent on an annual basis.
